newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch long bond yields dropped to their lowest closing levels in about seven months on Friday as sellers became thin on the ground, dealers said.

"There are not a lot of sellers out there but I don't think anyone is willing to go out a buy aggressively," said one dealer as the yield on the benchmark 10-year guilder bond, the January 2006 issue, ended just over the key six percent level.
Some repositioning was also reported over the yield curve, including buying in the longer end late in the day.
But dealers said few players were willing to take new positions ahead of important upcoming meetings.
European finance ministers are meeting this weekend in Dublin, while the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will on Tuesday consider the level of U.S. interest rates.
But a 25 basis point rise is also factored into prices.
"For Europe, it's a formality because Europe goes its own way. It's going up," said one dealer, attributing this to a lack of supply in longer maturities.
Another said he expected guilder paper to outperform bunds over the next few weeks, adding that he had seen British pension funds switching into the Netherlands market from Germany today.
